title: Feedback portfolio gaps and low-touch remediations — 2025-09-21
body:
Executive summary:

This is a compact synthesis of customer feedback collected across support threads, account reviews, and field interviews (Aug–Sep 2025). Purpose: produce a prioritized portfolio of gaps (small-medium technical and UX frictions) plus a set of low-touch remediation ideas that can be shipped quickly or used as mitigations while we scope larger work.

High-level takeaways:
- A small number of medium-impact runtime/observability gaps generate most friction and escalations (kv-cache invalidation edgecases, fallbacks between model variants, and opaque cost spikes).
- Customers want a mix of quick operational controls (toggle-able) and product changes (per-route throttle/prediction, clearer billing signals).
- Several asks can be addressed by ops/console fixes or short runtime patches (<= 2w eng effort).

Methodology / sources:
- 72 support tickets labelled "latency" / "cost-anomaly" (CS triage July–Sept).
- 12 enterprise scoping calls (accounts >$5k/mo).
- Internal field notes and SRE incident summaries (linked).
- Quick manual clustering (this doc is intentionally lightweight; use it to gate a follow-up scoped PRD).

Gap map (clustered by root cause, with representative customer quotes):

1) KV cache invalidation & cold-start oscillations (impact: High; frequency: Medium)
- Quote: "We see token cost jump and occasional doubled latency when we switch contexts — looks like cache misses." — mid-market analytics customer.
- Symptoms: interleaved requests from different sessions causing KV cache thrash; manual prefixes not preserved across model variant fallbacks.
- Suggested short-term/low-touch patches: add per-customer cache TTL override in Console (ops control), log and surface cache miss rate per-route in light-weight dashboard.
- Rough cost to implement: 2 engineer-weeks (serving-runtime + console).

2) Fallback model mapping transparency & predictable degradations (impact: Medium; frequency: High)
- Quote: "When our p99 model is overloaded it falls back to a smaller model and answers change — we need to know exactly which variant was used per call." — platform team at a SaaS customer.
- Symptoms: no token-level annotation in usage export about fallback model; rollouts lead to surprise quality deltas.
- Low-touch remediations: include a per-response header (model_variant_id) and add a per-route rollout preview with quality delta badges in Console.
- Cost: 1.5 engineer-weeks + 1 UX small task.

3) Sudden cost spikes from bursty chat workloads (impact: High; frequency: Low but high-severity)
- Quote: "One support campaign doubled our token spend overnight — unclear which prompts are the culprit."
- Observed: mixed long context + streaming + small bursts; missing per-prompt cost attribution makes triage slow.
- Low-touch remediations: enable optional prompt-level sampling tag (insert trace_id) and add a daily top-10 prompt footprint export. Also add soft budget alerts (Console) for per-route token burn rate.
- Cost: 2–3 engineer-weeks (exporting + alerting).

4) Confusing quantization/accuracy trade messaging (impact: Medium; frequency: Medium)
- Quote: "We tried the q4hf version and sometimes answers are wrong — the docs don't show when to avoid quantization."
- Symptoms: customers pick quantized model variants to save cost but run into hallucination/quality regressions for certain prompt types.
- Low-touch remediation: quick docs update with example prompts (do/don't), and a console warning when routing a route to quantized variants with a sample-quality indicator.
- Cost: docs + small console banner (~1 engineer-week + docs writer time).

Priority heatlist (quick wins first) — recommended ordering for a 6-week ops sprint:

A) Per-response variant annotation + export field (visibility) — high-value, low-effort (1.5w)
B) Console: per-route cache-miss metric + TTL override (2w)
C) Soft budget alerts + top prompt footprint daily export (2–3w)
D) Documentation + console warnings on quantization tradeoffs (1w)
E) Rollout preview with quality delta badges (2w)

Costed patches (ballpark estimates):
- A: 1.5 engineer-weeks (serving + downstream logging) — Moderate risk
- B: 2 engineer-weeks (runtime + console metric plumbing) — Low risk if we reuse existing metrics infra
- C: 2.5 engineer-weeks (billing/usage export tie-in + alerting UI) — Medium risk (billing schema involvement)
- D: 0.5–1 engineer-week + 2 docs-days — Very low risk
- E: 2 engineer-weeks + product review — Medium risk

Operational mitigations (to run in parallel while product work is scoped):
- Temp policy: offer per-account request-rate cap upon request (SRE-created rule) — immediate stopgap for cost spikes.
- Incident playbook update: add a "token burn triage" checklist for CS/ops to run on cost escalations.
- Script: nightly scan for routes with >3x baseline token burn and auto-ping account owners + CS.

Unresolved questions / unknowns:
- How much instrumentation effort to expose kv-cache miss rates with current metrics pipeline? (need infra input)
- Will annotations (model_variant_id header) affect downstream customers relying on raw response schema? (compat risk)
- Are there regulatory constraints on exposing per-request traces for certain enterprise customers? (legal check)

Quick prototype plan (MVP implementation steps):
1) Implement model_variant_id header in dev environment (serving-runtime PR + tests).
2) Add a small CSV export line for variant usage to the existing usage exporter.
3) Console: add a read-only metric card for cache misses and a TTL input under route settings.
4) Ship docs + help center article for quantization guidance.

Customer impact examples (synthesis):
- Customer A (fintech, $12k/mo): most frustrated by opaque fallbacks — made conservative decision to pin to a single model, hurting cost. Visibility would let them embrace automatic fallbacks safely.
- Customer B (marketplace, $2.3k/mo): overhead from prompt-level costs; happy to test a soft-alert beta.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Run a short instrument spike to see KV miss surface area (ask infra to enable a metric flag).
- [ ] Book a 30-min alignment with Product (Priya) and SRE (Liam) to confirm feasibility and ordering.
- [ ] Draft a small release note template for variant annotations (compat notice).
- [ ] Add a short CS playbook snippet for per-account soft caps.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts referenced:
- Confluence collection: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/feedback-collection-2025Q3
- Example support thread snippet: JIRA-4321 (ticket export attached separately)
- Runtime PR that spawned related discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987

——
If we want to move this to a scoped PRD: recommend a 2-week discovery sprint (1 engineer, 1 product, 1 SRE, 1 CS) to validate metric availability and finalize the wireframes for the Console cards. This doc is a lightweight starting point; feedback welcome.
